messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I ran a small canary for FlashAttention v3 on batch sizes 1/8/32 and saw a weird regression at seq_len=4096 with fused kernels.  ~10% p50 increase. Anyone else seeing this?
Maria: Hmm, saw something similar in local perf tests. v3 fused wins at 2k but regresses around 4k+ depending on kv layout. attaching quick numbers.
Maria: ```
# microbench (n=100)
model: llama-13b
hw: A100-80GB
seq  | batch=1  | batch=8   | batch=32
512  |  12ms    |  9ms      |  7ms
2048 |  38ms    |  28ms     |  24ms
4096 |  86ms    |  74ms     |  67ms  <-- v2: 78ms, v3: 86ms
```
Sam: That aligns with KV sharding behaviour — v3 fused kernel moves more work to the attention pass and relies on contiguous KV memory. On our paged-KV layout we get extra memcpy churn.
Jia: Important: we should distinguish two things in the plan: kernel selector heuristic (auto choose v2/v3/fused/paged) vs feature-flag rollout (force-enable for testing). Keep them separate.
Alex: Agreed. Propose a 3-stage approach: (1) offline perf matrix + selector rules, (2) feature-flagged canary (1% -> 10% -> 50%), (3) gated rollout with regression monitors and auto-fallback. Thoughts?
Leo: +1. Add a KV-sensitivity score to the selector: if kv_pages>threshold || non-contig_kv -> prefer v2 or paged-attn instead of fused. We have telemetry for kv_contiguity.
Maria: Also add a batching heuristic: fused is good when batch>4 and seq<3k; for long sequences pref v2/paged. I'll draft a decision table.
Sam: For canary, request these metrics from the runtime: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU SM util, memcpy bytes, kv memcpy rate. We'll set regression thresholds: p50 +6% OR p95 +8% OR memcpy bytes +15%.
Alex: Can you paste the fflag names we'll use? want to add to infra tickets.
Jia: Suggested flags: `ff_fa_v3_force`, `ff_fa_v3_selector_v2`, `ff_fa_v3_canary_pct`. Keep names short.
Leo: Important: implement a soft-fallback path in runtime — if selected kernel triggers memcpy spike, automatically switch to fallback for that request and emit a trace (no user-facing error). Metric to trigger fallback: memcpy delta > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive requests.
Maria: I ran a quick fused vs paged fused microbenchmark with KV paged layout — paged-attn (non-fused) keeps latency stable at 4096 but lower throughput. Summary: fused improves throughput for mid-length across batches, paged is safer for tail-latency.
Maria: ```
# paged vs fused (seq=4096, batch=8)
fused: p50 74ms, memcpy 1.8GB/s, tps 120
paged: p50 68ms, memcpy 0.9GB/s, tps 95
note: fused shows higher memcpy and occasional jitter
```
Sam: Could be memory fragmentation on CUDA side for fused when KV grows. I'll add a profiler run with nvprof and cupy memstats to confirm.
Leo: Ops ask: can we gate by model shape? Some customers pin seq_len and model type; selector should accept policy overrides per-customer.
Alex: Good call. We'll let Dedicated/Private override. Default selector picks by telemetry + conservative rules.
Jia: I'll sketch rollout playbook: 1% daytime traffic for 24h, check metrics, expand to 10% for 48h, run nightly long-seq stress tests, then 50% with auto-fallback enabled. Rollback if any rule trips.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/ff-fashattn-v3 at 1842002500 — canary gate off by default.
Alex: Thanks — next actions: Maria to publish selector table, Sam to attach profiler traces, Jia to create FF + infra tickets, Leo to add KV telemetry check.
Sam: I'll also add a small binary that can simulate paged vs contig KV to reproduce locally.
Maria: I'll aim to push the decision table by EOD. :eyes:
Alex: :thumbsup:
